D.t: Helena Foulkes leads by 15.6 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 66,517 votes; a one point swing is about 2,129 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +8.8 and D +22.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +8.6. Your best recent poll is University of New Hampshire at D +19.2; your worst is Emerson College/WPRI at D +9.7. 5 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Providence, a projected net 39,669 votes; Newport, a projected net 9,904 votes; Washington, a projected net 8,843 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Kent, D +1.7, 18.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Helena Foulkes runs furthest behind in Washington, Kent. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 86% of voters, 48 to 36, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.28 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 64% of voters, 53 to 32, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.18 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 53 to 33, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.11 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Helena Foulkes: Immigration voters 27 to 52, Independents 42 to 44, 2022 voters who skipped 2024 44 to 42. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$215K cash against $264K. Roughly even money; the air war will be decided by outside groups and earned media.
